event.tilda_heart5.0.text: Sit, [player]. Sit first, eat second, talk third. A dozen scones for a village that buys six, and you at my counter looking like a long night. I have the chair and the time.
event.tilda_heart5.0.why: frightened band: she gets gentler and feeds the player

event.tilda_heart5.0.text: Sit a moment. I baked a dozen scones for a village that buys six, and the street's been quiet all morning. Quiet enough to count.
event.tilda_heart5.0.why: uneasy: a Keeper's counting shows through

event.tilda_heart2.1.text: My mother's cauliflower gratin. She taught it by hand, never wrote it down. Most of what she gave me has no writing to it. Bring me a cauliflower someday.
event.tilda_heart2.1.why: clue: her mother handed down more than recipes

event.hall_dance.3.text: Nobody asked for credit for any of this. So I'm giving it, in the good chalk, under every name in this room. I counted the room twice. Everyone's here.
event.hall_dance.3.why: the Keeper headcount as relief; coin hinge (.10) untouched

event.story_notes_tilda.after.text: Signing a kindness is just sending a bill. ...Two more doors, then I'll walk you partway home. No arguing. The nights come in fast this time of year.
event.story_notes_tilda.after.why: frightened: 'don't follow me' becomes walking the player home

event.story_notes_tilda.after.text: Signing a kindness is just sending a bill. ...Two more doors before closing. Then home, both of us. The lamp's on upstairs if you ever need it.
event.story_notes_tilda.after.why: uneasy: the lamp tell, no imagery

dlg.story.scarecrow.talk.0.text: Mine is smiling. Crows can't stand a cheerful face. Not that there've been many crows this fall. Don't let that sway the judging.
dlg.story.scarecrow.talk.0.why: wakefulness ladder: birds quieter, played as comedy

event.festival_winter_lanterns.0.text: Lanterns up, everyone. Not lit yet. Wait for the bell, and keep hold of your string till it rings. Felix, I mean you.
event.festival_winter_lanterns.0.why: care that is too exact: hold the string

dlg.tilda.slate.0.text: This is the slate. Every small kindness in Wetherell, in chalk. There are columns I keep for people who can't collect anymore. I don't wipe those either.
dlg.tilda.slate.0.why: clue: echoes Edmund without naming him

dlg.tilda.hours.0.text: I count the stock at closing time. Lately the count comes out right, the street comes out short, and I leave the lamp burning longer.
dlg.tilda.hours.0.why: uneasy: the lamp burns longer as the street empties

dlg.tilda.hours.1.text: Wetherell holds, I tell myself. It costs what it costs, and it holds. ...Forget I said that. What do you think — is it shrinking?
dlg.tilda.hours.1.why: revelation slip-and-cover; still asks the choice question

event.tilda_heart6.after.text: Said out loud, it weighs less. Yours does too, whatever it is. Leave it on my counter with the rest. Turn the sign back, and take a scone for the walk.
event.tilda_heart6.after.why: frightened: Felix joke cut, she tends the player's dread instead

dlg.tilda.card.1.text: My mother's pumpkin pie. The only thing she ever wrote down. The rest of what she kept, I keep now, quietly. What if I get it wrong?
dlg.tilda.card.1.why: clue: the inheritance was a keeping, not a recipe

event.tilda_heart10.give.text: Pumpkin pie, still warm. Eat something, you. And yes, that's your farm on my sign. Supplier. In paint. Paint stays put, whatever else moves.
event.tilda_heart10.give.why: frightened: fixing the farm's name is protection; pie and sign kept

event.overheard_tilda_wren_2.l3.text: Then we'll trade. Yours first, and keep it cheerful. The street's been short on cheerful lately.
event.overheard_tilda_wren_2.l3.why: two Keepers rationing good news; Wren's reply still lands

event.overheard_tilda_wren_3.l3.text: One cup. It's the fourth. We both close early on the fourths.
event.overheard_tilda_wren_3.l3.why: hint: the fourths as a visible custom, Keeper to Keeper

event.overheard_tilda_wren_3.l3.text: One cup. Then back to the slate. Some nights the books keep me; you know the ones.
event.overheard_tilda_wren_3.l3.why: hint, any day: 'the books' covering the duty

event.overheard_tilda_juno_3.l2.text: Open it in Wetherell and I'll stock your first shelf. Stay close. The village does better full.
event.overheard_tilda_juno_3.l2.why: her need for a full village gains an edge; Juno's reply holds

adds.text: Eat one more. For the walk home. I'm not asking, I'm stocking you.
adds.why: fills the silence left by cutting .1; gentleness as provisioning

adds.text: Send them seaward. Never toward the wood. The wood keeps what it catches.
adds.why: hint-tier custom; reads as lanterns-in-trees to a calm player, agrees with Ione's sea drift

cuts.why: the Felix-flinches joke falls flat in a strained scene; paired with the add after .3
